title: eGarage Meta-Contract Schema v2
description: Validates any eGarage integration contract file in contracts/registry/. Architecture defined by ADR-000.

meta_description.description: Optional human-readable statement of what this contract represents.

id.description: Globally unique contract identifier. Format: {domain}.{contract-name}.v{major}. Examples: catalog.product-knowledge.v1, inventory.stock.v1

owner.description: Bounded context that owns and versions this contract.

publisher.description: Single subsystem responsible for publishing every Message Type in this contract.

write_authority.description: Sole subsystem authorized to write the governed data. Required non-null for Truth contracts. Must be null for all other categories.

message_types.description: Independently versioned messages belonging to this contract. Every contract must declare at least one Message Type. Contracts with a single message still use this array — there is no shorthand.

id.description: Globally unique Message Type identifier. Format: {domain}.{entity}.{action}. Examples: catalog.product.changed, inventory.stock.updated. IDs must be unique across the entire platform, not just within the parent contract.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of this message's business semantics.

version.description: SemVer of this Message Type's payload and behavior. Independent from the parent contract version. A breaking schema or semantic change requires a MAJOR increment.

schema_ref.description: Path to the JSON Schema that validates this Message Type's payload. Relative to contracts/.

interaction.description: Semantic interaction pattern of this Message Type. event: publisher emits without prior request. request-response: consumer requests, publisher responds. snapshot: complete domain state at emission time. stream: continuous flow, consumer subscribes. Changing interaction is a breaking change.

transport.description: Physical delivery mechanism. queue: message broker (Kafka, RabbitMQ, Django Q). http: REST or RPC endpoint. file: filesystem or object storage. grpc: gRPC channel. webhook: publisher calls consumer-registered URL. Changing transport is an implementation change, not a semantic breaking change.

frequency.description: Expected publication or availability cadence for this specific Message Type.

guarantees.description: Binding commitments from the publisher for this Message Type. Changing any guarantee — in any direction — is a breaking change.

idempotent.description: Whether a consumer can safely process the same message more than once without side effects.

ordered.description: Whether messages are guaranteed to arrive in the order they were published.

consistency.description: Data consistency model visible to consumers at delivery time.

completeness.description: Whether the payload represents a change (delta) or the complete current state (full-snapshot).

max_staleness.description: Maximum acceptable age of the delivered data. Format: '5m', '1h', '24h'. Null when staleness does not apply (e.g. on-demand or realtime).

consumers.description: Exhaustive list of authorized consumers. Unlisted subsystems are not authorized. Each consumer declares exactly which Message Types it consumes — declaring only the parent contract is not allowed. Cross-reference validation (consumer.message_types[] vs message_types[].id) is enforced by CI script, not by this schema.

subsystem.description: Identifier of the authorized consumer subsystem.

message_types.description: Message Type IDs this consumer is authorized to consume. Each ID must exist in the parent contract's message_types[].id list.

version.description: SemVer of this contract definition. Describes the contract collection and governance metadata. Independent from message_types[].version. Increment MAJOR when a message_type is added, removed, or renamed, or when owner/publisher changes.

status.description: draft: under design, must not be consumed in production. stable: approved for production. deprecated: replaced, consumers must migrate.

min_consumer_version.description: Minimum contract version consumers are expected to support. Null until a minimum is formally established.

pending_decisions.description: ADR identifiers that must reach Accepted before this contract can become stable. A non-empty list blocks transition to stable.
